title: Live-cell Imaging of Migrating Cells Expressing Fluorescently-tagged Proteins in a Three-dimensional Matrix
protocol: Plate cells at 80-90% confluency in a p35 dish.
Transfect the cells with the plasmid of interest using Lipofectamine 2000.
Passage the cells into two p150 petri dishes the next day.
Change the media and add 500 μg/ml of G418 to each dish the following day.
Change media every other day for approximately 2 weeks.
Identify GFP positive colonies using an inverted fluorescent microscope after 2 weeks.
Mark these colonies on the plate using a sharpie pen.
Aspirate out the media before selectively trypsinizing the colonies.
Wash the cells twice with PBS or trypsin solution.
Leave a thin layer of liquid on the bottom of the plate during the second wash.
Use a sterilized cotton swab to wipe around the edge of each colony on the plate.
Pipette 10 μl of trypsin onto each colony and pipette up and down several times to detach cells from the plate.
Transfer all detached cells from each colony into a single well in a 24-well dish.
Incubate plates at 37 °C for 5-10 minutes until cells appear round and are fully detached.
Pipette 10 μl of trypsin onto each colony to detach the cells.
Transfer all cells from each colony into a single well in a 24-well dish.
Incubate glass bottom dishes with 300 μl of 2% 3-Aminopropyltrimethoxysilane solution for 1 hour at room temperature.
Aspirate out the 3-Aminopropyltrimethoxysilane solution from each dish.
Wash each dish three times with filtered water, each wash lasting 10 minutes.
Aspirate out the water.
Place dishes on hot plate set to 50 °C for 1.5 hours with tops slightly off the dish.
Remove dishes from heat and allow to cool.
Pipette 300 μl of 2% glutaraldehyde solution diluted in PBS onto each dish.
Incubate for 1 hour.
Aspirate out the glutaraldehyde solution.
Wash dishes with PBS three times for 10 minutes each.
Sterilize dishes by exposure to UV light for 1 hour.
Pipette 240 μl of growth media into an eppendorf tube.
Add 12.6 μl of 1M Hepes and 20 μl of filtered water to the media.
Add 50 μl of cell solution containing approximately 2 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Add 10 μl of fluorescent particles resuspended in 30 μl of media.
Add 167 μl of bovine dermis Collagen I solution (to obtain a working concentration of 1 mg/ml).
Mix the solution thoroughly.
Pipette 80 μl of the mixed collagen gel onto the glass portion of the silanized glass bottom dish.
Place dish into incubator and allow the gel to polymerize at 37 °C for 30 minutes.
Add 2 ml of growth media carefully to each dish.
Turn on the temperature control of the microscope enclosure.
Let the scope chamber equilibrate to a steady state temperature of 37 °C.
Change media to new media supplemented with 25 mM Hepes.
Exchange the top of the dish for one that has a glass top if DIC imaging is required.
Cover the side of the dish with a thin strip of parafilm to prevent media evaporation.
Place one drop of immersion fluid on the objective for an oil immersion objective.
Place the collagen gel containing dish on microscope stage.
Make sure the dish makes contact with the immersion liquid.
Focus the sample and search for cells of interest to image.
Allow the dish to settle for about 45 minutes before starting a long capture.
Specify the parameters of image acquisition.
Modulate laser power, exposure time, frequency, and duration of capture time to minimize laser exposure.
Add an inhibitor during the time-lapse acquisition if required.
Do not seal the dish with parafilm for inhibitor addition experiments.
Prepare Hepes supplemented media with drug at a desired working concentration.
Pause the image capture when ready to add drug to media.
Carefully remove the dish top without disturbing the dish.
Aspirate out the media in the dish.
Pipette the drug containing media into the dish.
Replace the dish top carefully.
Readjust the focus if the sample is out-of-focus due to new media addition.
Restart the image capture.
Monitor the capture for the next 30 minutes.
Readjust the focus as necessary.
Continue capture.
Ensure recovery time is sufficient to capture full fluorescence recovery.
Measure average fluorescent intensity of photobleached area before and after photobleaching over time.
Fit the recovery curve to the exponential equation I=If(1-e-kt) using statistical analysis software.
Determine half-time (τ½) from the equation τ½=ln(2)/k.
Obtain parameters including half-time and final intensity from the fitted curve.
Calculate mobile fraction by taking the ratio of final fluorescence intensity to initial fluorescence intensity.
Photobleach the region of interest using optimized laser settings.
Acquire post-FRAP images with controlled exposure and time intervals.
Quantify background photobleaching if significant during image acquisition.
Define the photobleached volume by taking pre and post 3D-stack images of the photobleached region.
Prepare a polymerized collagen matrix on a glass-bottom dish.
Treat the glass bottom dish with 3-Aminopropyltrimethoxysilane solution.
Crosslink the collagen matrix by treating it with glutaraldehyde solution.
